topic: Brown and Cameron's irrational purely imaginary independence-root question and the classification of rational squared imaginary parts
title: Extending Brown and Cameron's classification of purely imaginary independence roots

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending Brown and Cameron's rational classification (2020, arXiv:2001.08881v2, Proposition 2.9, p. 8), we answer their Question 2 (p. 11) affirmatively and classify all purely imaginary independence roots whose imaginary part has rational square: they are exactly ±i/√n for positive integers n. An explicit connected graph of independence number four realizes each pair. A second graph whose independence polynomial takes the value one at these roots gives connected examples of every independence number at least four and connected induced supergraphs of arbitrary finite graphs. Bencs's tree-transfer theorem gives infinitely many trees for each pair. A smaller 128-vertex example realizes ±i/√2.
summary: The rational-root obstruction and an explicit 108n²-vertex construction classify all rational squared imaginary parts. A companion join construction yields connected examples of every independence number at least four and induced connected supergraphs of arbitrary finite graphs. Bencs's theorem supplies infinitely many trees for each pair. A 128-vertex witness and precise finite and Lean statement coverage are included.
